name: Dermalinfusion

card.summary: Branded exfoliate-and-infuse facial with one small published study on hyperpigmentation.

quick.overview:
Dermalinfusion pairs skin exfoliation with serum infusion in one pass. It is offered as a facial treatment.

The only publication found examined it alongside a peptide for dark marks after inflammation in darker skin.
quick.mechanism: A handheld tip is described as exfoliating while delivering a serum to the skin.
quick.risks: No safety information was available in the sources reviewed.

lead: Dermalinfusion is a branded in-clinic facial that pairs particle-free exfoliation with the simultaneous delivery of skin-care serums. People have it done to smooth skin texture, clean pores and give the skin a fresher, more hydrated look before photos or events.[1]

A UC Davis Health otolaryngology skin-care page describes the Silk Peel Dermalinfusion version as a more advanced take on microdermabrasion: a medical-grade diamond exfoliator resurfaces the skin and cleanses pores, then a patented infusion process delivers products chosen for the person's skin type, which the page says plump the tissue. The page states that many patients notice improvement after one treatment.[1]

The published literature is a brief 2014 note in the Journal of Drugs in Dermatology by Bhatia, Hsu and Hantash on combined topical delivery and dermalinfusion of decapeptide-12 for post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation in skin of color.[2]

chain: Diamond-tip exfoliation removes dead surface cells
Serums are infused in the same pass
angle.text: A provider passes a handheld tip over the face that exfoliates and delivers a serum in one step, aiming for smoother texture, cleaner pores and a hydrated, fresh appearance.

infobox: Handheld diamond-tip device in a clinic

paras: Provider pages describe a particle-free exfoliation, in contrast to crystal microdermabrasion, followed or accompanied by infusion of serums selected for skin type.[1] Branded variants and names differ between clinics.

A 2014 note in the Journal of Drugs in Dermatology reported on combined topical delivery and dermalinfusion of decapeptide-12 to speed resolution of post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation in skin of color.[2] No other studies were found.

timeline.event: Journal of Drugs in Dermatology note on dermalinfusion of decapeptide-12 for post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation.[2]
